title: An explicit list limit loses a clinical write, or an unbounded list exhausts the service
hazard: A request carrying a legitimate long clinical list is refused before it is recorded, or a missing bound lets a caller consume enough memory or processing time to delay other care
cause: The shared limit is too small for a real record; a nested array escapes the check; the OpenAPI document omits or overstates a maximum; a future PATCH appends arrays or confuses absent with null
effect: Clinical information is not recorded when expected, or the service is unavailable while a clinician needs the record
controls: Every OpenAPI array schema states maxItems, with smaller domain limits preserved and 1,000 otherwise; a census walks nested schemas and catches a planted omission. Before a handler can append a version, middleware recursively walks every JSON request array and refuses more than 1,000 as 422, naming only its dotted field and the limit; boundary tests cover 1,000 and 1,001 nested items. Updates remain whole append-only versions. There is no PATCH route, and a census guard requires any future PATCH to declare absent-keeps, null-clears and no implicit array append semantics.
residual: The 1,000-item default is an engineering choice no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer reviewed; a legitimate list above it is refused and must be split only where the domain offers a supported route; smaller field-specific limits are enforced by their existing domain validators, not the shared middleware; responses are not independently checked against maxItems; no PATCH exists to exercise the future guard

title: Two different people are linked as one
hazard: A new registration or an import is auto-linked to another person's record
cause: Matcher false positive: similar names and birth dates, shared address, a typo that makes two national health numbers collide, twins
effect: Clinician sees, and writes to, another person's identity record; later clinical content would be attributed to the wrong person
controls: Twins never AutoLink; two different valid national health numbers are NonMatch; a missing given name, family name or birth date blocks AutoLink; absent evidence is None not zero; review band routes to a person; duplicate check at registration needs a written override reason; compare is symmetric, so the order in which two records are compared never changes the decision (given names of equal length are averaged both ways and the lower kept); a repeated-digit national health number (0000000000 and the like) is a placeholder, invalid, and never decides a link; a shared national health number with both given and family names disagreeing goes to Review; a shared national health number with two different full birth dates always goes to Review, however close the dates; birth-date typo credit only for a one-digit slip or an adjacent swap (a parent and child sharing a birthday score 0), and an impossible date is absent; a given name that folds to nothing (a dash, spaces) is absent, not a disagreement; the service uses matcher 0.4.0 (published 2026-10-26), which carries all of these controls and CQ-37, and refuses a placeholder national health number at registration; since 0.3.0 (CQ-19) a given name on one record that nothing on the other matches (John against John Paul) blocks AutoLink, and a family name of several parts is compared part by part so Smith-Jones does not match Smithson; a name is also compared transliterated (Müller as Mueller, José as Jose), taking the better score, which can raise a similarity but never lowers one and leaves other scripts alone; given and family names keyed into each other's boxes (Taylor Morgan against Morgan Taylor) are scored at 0.9 of their similarity and blocked from AutoLink with a stated conflict, so they go to Review; a combining mark (virama, vowel sign) stays with its letter, so an Indic or Persian name is one word, not several fragments; phone numbers are compared in E.164 form (07700 900123 and +44 7700 900123 are one number) and a number under 7 digits is absent, not a match; a shared postcode, or a shared phone with no shared email, counts at half weight as household evidence, so relatives at one address are not lifted toward a link; a nickname and its formal name (Bill, William) score 0.8, under the given-name auto-link minimum, so they reach Review and never link on the name alone; a pair the spelling scores as unrelated but whose family and first given name sound alike (Soundex), with the same birth date, goes to Review with a stated conflict, the score unchanged; a placeholder name (Unknown, Unidentified, Anonymous, UNK-nnn) is absent evidence, so two unidentified patients never match each other and an unidentified patient never auto-links to a real record; the registration and compare pages show each reason a link cannot be automatic from its stable code in the page's language, falling back to the matcher's English text for a code they do not know (CQ-38; the nine-locale wording is machine-written and unreviewed); (matcher 0.4.0, CQ-37) a shared valid national health number with a given name, family name or birth date absent on either record goes to Review, not AutoLink; no code of the service links two records by itself, held by a test (2026-11-25, AG-8); in matcher 0.9.0, which the service uses, no pair is AutoLink without a verified identifier that both records carry, whatever the configuration (2026-11-25, AG-13); the screens say Very alike, a person must decide, and no longer Automatic link (2026-11-25, AG-13)
residual: Thresholds (auto_link 0.92, review 0.75) are unvalidated guesses with no real-data evaluation; there is no merge yet (ID-5) so no auto-link is performed by the service. Gap found 2026-10-23 (CQ-30, CQ-37): a shared valid national health number linked automatically even with no names or birth date present. Decided 2026-10-25 (maintainer; the Clinical Safety Officer has not reviewed it): a missing given name, family name or birth date now sends a shared-number pair to Review, in matcher 0.4.0 (tests/properties.rs::a_shared_national_number_alone_goes_to_review), published 2026-10-26 and used by the service. Added 2026-10-25: no clinician has retested the CQ-19 rules (part-by-part family names, nicknames, phonetic Review, swap) against the service now that it runs 0.4.0, and the thresholds were not re-evaluated; the translated reasons are machine-written and no speaker has reviewed them. The matcher can now weigh a shared date of death as weak evidence (0.05, OQ-BV3); two people who die on one day gain a little score; the service uses this only on a merge, from a standing and undisputed assertion, and never accepts it from a client (2026-11-05); a postcode or a telephone number that many people share (a prison, a barracks, a hostel, a care home) is counted as evidence about one person: two people with one birth date and nothing else in common reach Review by sharing both (2026-11-25, XP-5); more pairs go to a person than before 0.9.0, and how many was not measured

title: A duplicate record is created
hazard: A person is registered again although a record exists
cause: Candidate search only finds records sharing a family name, a birth date or an identifier; a re-registration with all three different (name change, wrong birth date) is not a candidate; two registrations of one person at the same moment (two clerks, a clerk and the HL7 feed, two feed connections) each passing the check before the other was stored
effect: Split history: information entered on one record is missing on the other; allergies or alerts not seen
controls: Duplicate check at registration with side-by-side view and override reason; search by name, birth date and identifier; the duplicate check, the insert and the audit row run in one transaction under a registration lock, for registration by a person and by the HL7 feed alike, so concurrent registrations of one person cannot both pass; candidates are ranked by evidence (a shared identifier, then family name and birth date together) before the 200 limit, and a cut list is reported; the register form ignores a second click while one request is in flight (CQ-33), so a double click cannot post the same registration twice; a national number is looked up without its spaces and hyphens by registration, search and the HL7 feed (2026-11-25, AG-12); the duplicate check also looks by a family name without case, accents, spaces and hyphens, by part of a double name, and by names or a birth date the other way round (2026-11-25, AG-12)
residual: Documented blind spot (nothing in common is not a candidate); no phonetic search; no merge or unmerge to repair a split (ID-5); when more than 200 records share a birth date or family name only the 200 strongest are compared: one sharing an identifier, or the family name and birth date, always is, but one sharing only a name or only a birth date (a mistyped birth date, say) can be cut; the registration page then says so, while an HL7 create only records it in the audit row; 3 of 19 synthetic kinds of duplicate are never looked at, and more candidates may mean more registrations held for a person, not measured (spec/patient-identity/candidate-recall.md)

title: An invalid or mistyped national health number is accepted
hazard: An identifier is stored that does not belong to the person
cause: Typing error that still passes, or an invalid number entered
effect: Wrong-patient lookup or failed lookup on an external system
controls: Modulus-11 check on every national health number at create and update; HL7 and FHIR inputs go through the same validation
residual: A valid-looking wrong number still passes; no PDS (national service) trace exists

title: An edit overwrites a newer edit
hazard: Two people change the same record and one change is lost
cause: Concurrent edit without a version check
effect: Correct demographics replaced by stale ones
controls: Append-only versions with optimistic expected_version (409 on stale, one winner in a race); FHIR update requires If-Match (428/412)
residual: UI shows the conflict but does not merge field by field

title: A record is shown to someone not entitled
hazard: A user reads identity data they should not
cause: Error in the unreviewed role and purpose permission table; a route missing from the table; a relationship wrongly recorded
effect: Confidentiality breach; loss of trust; legal exposure
controls: Route gate refuses any route not in the table (census test); record-level decision on role, relationship, purpose and consent; every read audited; refusals audited; a role whose permissions come only from a view (vaccinator, WL-7, 2026-11-09) reads and searches only the kinds of record its view in electronic-patient-record-domain/src/role_views.toml names, and a bad view file is refused (tests/http_role_views.rs)
residual: The permission table is a first draft and has not been reviewed by a clinical safety officer or a privacy officer; the service does not verify that a token sub is the patient it is linked to

title: A patient's consent refusal is ignored
hazard: A record is disclosed after the patient refused
cause: Consent not applied on some path (search, duplicate check, FHIR, a future export)
effect: Breach of the patient's choice; breach of law for Part 2 data
controls: Consent applied on identity read, search (hidden results dropped, counted only in the audit row) and the duplicate check; a deny always wins; an unreadable provision denies; FHIR endpoints run the same handlers; a refusal on a record merged into another stands for the survivor, and its audit row names the merged-in record (WL-2, 2026-11-09, tests/http_roles.rs); a consent that says what another in force says is refused, also for two writers at one moment, so that withdrawing it withdraws it (2026-11-25); only refusals follow a merge, and a permission is asked for again on the record that stands (2026-11-25, OQ-AG14)
residual: No bulk export, clinical content or UI for consent exists yet; each new read path must be checked against this hazard; the national data opt-out service is local only; a refusal on a record merged into this one counts and is not in this record's list, so it is withdrawn on that record; consents doubled before 2026-11-25 stand until each is withdrawn

title: Sensitive information is shown unmasked
hazard: Substance-use, HIV, psychiatric or restricted data appears to staff without a need
cause: Security labels not enforced when clinical content arrives
effect: Harm to the patient (discrimination, safety); breach of 42 CFR Part 2 style rules
controls: The policy engine decides on labels and a general permit never unmasks SUD; entries of the problem list, relative history and typing can carry a label, and one that a reader may not see is withheld by the store from every route of those lists (2026-11-25); who adds and who lifts a label is decided and is a library (2026-11-25, OQ-PI7); someone outside the care team cannot tell that anything is withheld (OQ-PI5)
residual: Nothing else can carry a label (allergies, observations, results, referrals, letters), so sensitive content there is shown to every role that reads it; the hazard is no longer latent and must be re-assessed; break-glass shows everything, substance use included, to any treating role (2026-11-25, OQ-PI2), so from the day a label is stored what limits it is the reason, the flag and the review; that is to be re-assessed by the Clinical Safety Officer, and has had no legal review

title: A clinician cannot see a record in an emergency
hazard: Care is delayed because access is refused
cause: A clinician has no care relationship with a patient in an emergency; break-the-glass was not built (now built, see H-024)
effect: Delayed treatment
controls: Break-the-glass (SE-3): a treating clinician with no care relationship is refused with an offer, gives a reason and acknowledges, and reads clinical content for 4 hours; purpose emergency is still not offered in the staff picker; where EPR_REQUIRE_PERMISSION_BASIS is on (WL-4, off by default) a clinical read without a basis is refused, and could-not-ask:emergency or could-not-ask:unconscious is always a basis, so the requirement never needs the patient's answer (tests/http_permission_basis.rs); the UI does not send a basis yet, so turning it on refuses every clinical read through the UI
residual: Care can still be delayed by the extra steps (a reason, a tick) and by a patient's refusal of consent, which break-the-glass deliberately does not lift; only reads of clinical content are opened (a clinician still cannot record without a relationship); the screens are English only; ratings are unreviewed

title: The audit trail is altered or truncated unnoticed
hazard: Access is hidden or evidence is lost
cause: Someone with database access edits or deletes audit rows, or the chain is unkeyed
effect: Misuse cannot be shown; patients are told a false access history
controls: Append-only table with triggers; hash chain, keyed MAC when EPR_INTEGRITY_MAC_KEY is set; verify endpoint; a head checkpoint detects removed newest rows; an unheld key is reported as a key problem not tampering
residual: The key is optional (unkeyed chain by default); nothing stores the head checkpoint for the operator; removed newest rows are undetected without one

title: An access happens without an audit row
hazard: An access is not recorded
cause: Audit write fails and the request still answers; a path forgets to audit
effect: Misuse cannot be shown
controls: Handlers audit before the data leaves and answer 500 if the row cannot be written; patient, consent and relationship writes and their audit row are one transaction, so a write that cannot be audited does not happen; refusals are audited
residual: A refusal row that cannot be written is logged only; 401, 400 and 422 responses are not audited; reads, refusals and the verify and search rows are audited in their own transactions

title: A relationship wrongly gives access
hazard: A person is linked as the patient, a proxy or care team of someone they are not
cause: Wrong subject recorded by an administrator; a stale link not ended
effect: Disclosure to the wrong person, including through the patient's own view
controls: Only clinical-admin can record relationships; ending is a new version; every change is audited; the patient's access log shows who looked; a proxy reads only the scopes its terms list and only until its expiry, and a proxy without terms reads nothing (PA-5); one person has one standing relationship of a kind with a patient at a time, also for two administrators at one moment, so that ending it ends the access (2026-11-25)
residual: No second person approves a link; no check that the subject is who the administrator says; the proxy scopes and the five-year limit are guesses no clinician has reviewed; no rule yet for a child who becomes able to decide for themself (adolescent confidentiality); relationships doubled before 2026-11-25 stand until each is ended, and nothing lists them; a person with two logins is two people here

title: Data from another system is stored wrongly
hazard: An HL7 or FHIR message becomes the wrong identity record
cause: A misparsed date or sex, a dropped element, an identifier given no system
effect: Wrong demographics under a right id, or an unusable record
controls: FHIR input with elements the record cannot hold is refused (422); unreadable HL7 date or sex is left blank with a warning; identifiers without an authority are skipped with a warning; HL7 AE/AR acknowledgements
residual: No conformance run; HL7 has no listener yet; HL7 reads MSH and PID only

title: The patient's access log misleads
hazard: The patient is told something false about who looked
cause: Roles are what the token said; older rows have no role; refused attempts shown as access
effect: Wrong belief that a record was or was not seen
controls: Entries say staff with the recorded role and organisation, never a name; refusals are labelled as refused; older entries say only staff; an access to a merged chart is recorded against the chart that was opened, whichever record its first row came from, so the survivor's log has it; the records that contributed are named beside it for an auditor and are not in the patient-facing log (tests/audit_attribution.rs, 2026-11-25, AG-6)
residual: Roles are not checked against a directory; no filter or date range; rows written before 2026-11-25 keep the first row's patient; a person whose record was merged in by mistake does not see, in their own log, that it was read through another chart (OQ-AG6)

title: A translated screen is wrong
hazard: A clinician or patient misreads an instruction
cause: Machine-written translations used in the interface
effect: Misunderstanding of a warning or a choice
controls: Translations are marked machine-written until a speaker reviews them; the default English is the reference
residual: No translation has been reviewed by a speaker

title: The system is used for real care although it is not ready
hazard: A site relies on a scaffold
cause: Overstated documentation or a deployment ignoring the warnings
effect: Any of the above, without safeguards
controls: Every README and AGENTS.md says not for clinical use; no clinical content exists; nothing claims certification or compliance
residual: No release gate stops a deployment; the clinical safety officer is not named (OQ-2)

title: The patient banner misleads
hazard: A clinician acts on the wrong person, age or allergy status shown in the banner
cause: Banner built from unsaved form input; a wrong or approximate age; an empty allergy line read as no allergies; a stale view after another user's edit; the previous patient's banner or allergies left on screen, or a late answer for them shown, after moving to another patient
effect: Treatment for the wrong person, or an allergy missed because it was read as absent
controls: The banner renders only the record as stored, never the form being edited; age is whole years or months from a full date, marked about for a partial date, and absent rather than guessed for an unreadable or future date; allergies always read Not recorded in this system and that this does not mean there are none; a record with little on it says what is missing; the version is shown beside the form and a stale save is refused; on moving to another patient the page clears the previous patient's record, allergies, form, photo and emergency-access notice at once, and every answer (record, allergies, look, save, photo) is dropped unless it is for the patient now on screen and is the latest asked for; the patient page shows when the record was last read and, if the latest background look failed or none succeeded for 2.5 minutes, an alert that it may not be current (the record stays on screen); the age is counted on the site's calendar day (the service's EPR_SITE_TIME_ZONE, an IANA name checked at start-up, UTC when unset), so every reader at a site sees the same age and it changes at the site's midnight, not UTC's; the no known allergies" statement's time is shown on the site's clock with the UTC time beside it (2026-10-26)"
evidence: electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/src/lib/PatientBanner.svelte;electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/tests/unit/patient.test.ts;electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/tests/e2e/patients.spec.ts;electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/src/routes/patients/[id]/+page.svelte;electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/tests/unit/data-age.test.ts;electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/tests/unit/time-zones.test.ts;electronic-patient-record-service-with-rust/electronic-patient-record-domain/src/site.rs; electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/tests/unit/patient-banner.test.ts::never reads as no allergies while they are unknown; electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/tests/unit/patient.test.ts::marks a partial birth date approximate and refuses what it cannot read
residual: The banner does not refresh when someone else edits while it is open (it reloads only on a conflict); no photo exists; the allergy line is a placeholder until allergies are recorded (RC-5) and must then be revisited; ages near midnight use UTC dates. The data-age notice is on the patient page only (not my-record, lists or the compare page); the 2.5-minute limit is a guess; it was tested with a stubbed API, not a real outage. Added 2026-10-25: the site zone is one per service, so a service covering sites in different zones counts every age on one zone's day; an older API that sends no zone leaves the UI on UTC; the setting is not validated against where the patient is; an older API that sends no zone leaves these times in UTC (still labelled UTC); no clinician has reviewed the rule

title: A patient photo is wrong or hostile
hazard: The banner shows another person's face, or an uploaded file harms a viewer
cause: A photo uploaded to the wrong record; an outdated photo; a file that is not an image (script in an SVG, a polyglot); a photo kept in a shared cache
effect: A clinician trusts the face and treats the wrong person; or the viewer's browser runs attacker content
controls: Only PNG and JPEG are stored, decided from the file bytes and not the claimed type, at most 512 KiB, never decoded or resized by the server; served nosniff with a sandboxing CSP and no-store; the photo is identity data under the same role, relationship, purpose and consent rules and every read and write is audited (the write in one transaction with its audit row); uploads carry the version last seen so a stale write is refused; removing a photo is a new version and the history stays; the banner always shows the photo of the stored current version; the photo is shown beside the name, birth date and national health number so a mismatch is visible
residual: Nothing checks that the photo is of this patient or even of a face; no virus or content scan; an image with hostile metadata is stored as is (never parsed here, but a downstream viewer may parse it); the client must not be trusted to size or type-check; old photo versions stay in backups

title: Allergy information is missing, stale or read as none
hazard: A clinician gives or prescribes something the patient reacts to, because the banner or list did not warn
cause: Allergies never recorded; a stated no-known-allergies that is out of date; an allergy ended or retracted wrongly; the viewing role or relationship is refused; the call fails; the criticality is not stated
effect: Anaphylaxis or other serious harm
controls: Every state where the system does not know says so in words and adds that this does not mean there are none (not recorded, not shown to you, could not be loaded); none known is only shown when a named clinician stated it at a time and nothing has been recorded since, and it cannot be stated while an active allergy exists; an active allergy always outranks a statement; high-criticality allergies lead the list and are marked; a risk that was not stated is not shown as low; the banner and the list share one answer; entered in error is final and only a clinician may set it; every version, author and reason is kept and nothing is deleted
residual: Only a thin allergy record exists: no drug-class or cross-reactivity (OR-6), no coded medicines list, no alert at prescribing, no second-person check, no reconciliation with other systems; the SNOMED check is shape-only; substances are free text so the same allergy can be recorded twice in different words; the banner reloads once a minute so a change is not instant

title: An allergy is ended or retracted wrongly
hazard: A real allergy stops being shown
cause: Marking an allergy no longer applies or entered in error by mistake, by the wrong person, or on the wrong patient
effect: The warning disappears and the patient is exposed
controls: Ending is a new version and entered in error is a separate permission held by clinicians, not nurses; both need the version last seen; the whole history with author and reason stays and is visible to an auditor; every change is audited with its patient in one transaction; an ended allergy still counts as a record so none known is not claimed
residual: No confirmation step in the page; no alert to the patient or a pharmacist when an allergy is ended; reading the history of an allergy has no screen yet (only the audit trail and the database)

title: Two different people are merged, or a merge hides information
hazard: One person's record is treated as another's after a merge, or something recorded against one is lost from view
cause: An administrator merges records of different people; a merge of look-alike records; allergies or consent not following the merge; an old record still edited
effect: Treatment of one person on another's allergies and history; a consent refusal ignored; information lost
controls: A merge is a link, never a rewrite: nothing is deleted or moved, so unmerging restores both records exactly (checked by a property test against a model); only the clinical-admin role may merge, with a required reason; the matcher must not call the pair a non-match, and two different verified national health numbers always refuse; the surviving record shows the merged-in allergies (each still naming the record it was made on) and a consent refusal on either record applies to both; the old record is read-only, says where it went in its banner, search and the duplicate check; a care relationship does not carry over; merges are serialised and cannot cycle; every merge and unmerge is audited in one transaction with the matcher verdict
residual: The matcher threshold is an unvalidated guess; nothing asks a second person to confirm a merge; there is no review queue of uncertain pairs (a person has to find them); only allergies, consent and identity follow a merge today, and every new kind of clinical content must be taught to follow it or it will silently stay on the old record; photos and relationships do not follow; the surviving record's no-known-allergies statement is not combined with the old record's

title: An HL7 feed writes the wrong demographics, or the port is open to anyone
hazard: A patient record is created or changed by a message that should not have been applied
cause: A misconfigured or hostile sender; a feed bound beyond the machine; a mis-mapped field; a message for the wrong person; MLLP has no authentication
effect: Wrong identity data under a right patient, a duplicate record, or an attacker rewriting names
controls: The listener is off unless EPR_MLLP_BIND is set, refuses a non-loopback address without an explicit allow, and refuses to start on any bad setting; the audit agent is configured and the peer address recorded, nothing the sender claims is trusted; the feed's role may only create and update identity (checked by the policy engine, never read or export); matching is on identifiers and an ambiguous match is refused; a possible duplicate is refused rather than created; an update never blanks a field, and never changes a birth date or national health number; a repeat writes nothing; the write and its audit row are one transaction; size, connection and idle limits; TLS on the port when configured (rustls, nothing in plain text then) and, with a client CA, only senders holding a certificate from it (IH-10), and with client names only a certificate valid for one of them, whose name is on every audit row (IH-6); a written method for taking a feed live (replay a sample and compare, a signed register of differences, one feed at a time, the old route kept; operations/hl7/going-live.md, IH-12, never used); unreadable streams close; a refused message is kept in a work queue (feed_refusals) that a clinical administrator reads and closes with an outcome and a reason, each step audited; a refusal kept in that queue is answered AR (do not resend, IH-1) and AE only when a resend can help, so a sender neither loops nor holds later messages behind it; a resend of a waiting message adds no row
residual: No authentication or encryption on MLLP itself; the deployer must provide a TLS terminator or private network; the work queue has a screen but no alert and no age limit, so a refusal nobody looks at waits and the sender may have stopped holding the message; the integrator role can now also create and update identity over the REST API; a wrong name from a trusted feed is applied (the first name is replaced); an A08 for a record that was merged away is treated as a new patient and then refused as a possible duplicate; no conformance testing with a real sender

title: Allergy data read through FHIR is taken to mean there are none
hazard: An outside system reads an empty or partial AllergyIntolerance result as "no allergies" and a clinician acts on it
cause: An empty or inactive-only search result; a consumer ignoring the OperationOutcome entry; a 403 or consent refusal shown as an empty list; an allergy entered in error left out; verification status and type not recorded; allergy under the surviving record after a merge
effect: A drug or food given to a person with an allergy the other system did not show
controls: An empty result always carries an OperationOutcome saying it does not mean there are none; only a standing clinician statement is exported as SNOMED 716186003 no known allergy; a refusal is an error with the same sentence, never an empty bundle; unstated criticality is omitted, never low; verificationStatus and type are omitted, not guessed; the result is checked against the typed R4 model; the same handler applies the gate, care relationship, purpose, consent and audit as the REST route; a recorded code is withheld from the FHIR export, because only its shape was checked, and a note says so; the mismatch of penicillin with the code for myocardial infarction is a negative test (2026-11-25, AG-3); a receiver can ask for the allergies and the vital signs entered in error alone, each saying only that it is withdrawn and none of its words, with a warning that it is not the patient's list; any other value of that parameter is refused (2026-11-25, AG-3)
residual: No UK Core or US Core profile validation and no HAPI run; a consumer can still ignore the outcome entry; no read by id and no write; a consumer learns of an allergy entered in error only if it asks, and nothing tells it to; one it took under another record before an unmerge is not among them; ratings are unreviewed; a receiver that reads only codes finds none for any allergy and may take that as nothing to check (OQ-AG3)

title: A refused HL7 message is never seen, or its text is seen by the wrong person
hazard: A patient's registration or correction sent by another system is refused and then lost, or the stored message is read by someone who should not see it
cause: Nobody works the queue; the queue has no screen or alert; a refusal closed as dismissed in error; the stored message is patient data for a person who may not be on record
effect: Wrong or missing demographics persist; a clinician works from a record that never received an update; a disclosure of a message text
controls: Each refusal is stored as received in append-only tables and stays until a person closes it once, with an outcome and a reason, and the closing is audited; only the clinical administrator role may read or close the queue (policy FeedQueue); a listing carries no message text and each read of a message is audited by id, never by content; the refusal is also in the audit trail; an administrator screen (/admin/feed) lists the open entries, shows a message on request and closes it with an outcome and a required reason; the navigation shows how many are waiting on the admin pages; a sender's resends of one message are one entry, not many (IH-1); the feed's health is judged every minute by the site's day, evening and weekend windows: open or recent refusals make it a warning, silence past the window or many refusals critical, no data unknown; each change is stored and logged once and served as a gauge and at /api/feed/health (IH-8)
residual: The count shows only on the admin pages (an administrator who never opens one never sees it), with no alert, no count on the home page and no age limit, so an unseen refusal is silent; messages are stored as plain text in the database like other patient data; "handled" is the closer's word and is not checked against the record; a temporary failure is not queued; ratings are unreviewed

title: Break-the-glass is used without need, or never reviewed
hazard: A clinician opens a patient's record without a clinical reason, or a misuse goes unnoticed
cause: A reason typed to get past the prompt; a grant used for curiosity; nobody reviews the queue; there is no real-time notification to a privacy officer; a reviewer who is a friend of the clinician
effect: A patient's confidential information is disclosed to someone with no care duty; the misuse is found late or never
controls: A mandatory reason and acknowledgement; a fixed 4-hour grant that asking again does not extend; only treating roles; the grant lifts the missing care relationship and every label, for reads of clinical content (not writes, not an export, not a patient's refusal of consent); every audit row of the access is flagged break-glass and names the grant; the patient sees that it happened in their access log; every grant waits in an unreviewed queue for the auditor role, once, with a note, and not by the person who opened it; append-only tables; the grant's start and expiry are shown on the site's clock with the UTC time beside it (2026-10-26), so staff at a site read the same expiry; two requests at one moment open one grant, so that asking twice neither extends it nor leaves two to review (2026-11-25)
residual: No real-time notification (nothing can send one); no count or alert for the review queue, so it is silent until the auditor opens the page; the reason is free text and is not checked; nothing detects patterns such as one clinician opening many grants; a grant lasts 4 hours with no way to end it early; a grant shows everything, labelled entries included by the decision of 2026-11-25 (OQ-PI2), so a misuse can disclose more; nothing asks whether a life or a limb is at risk (FR-4.6, PI-10); ratings are unreviewed

title: A session stays open on an unattended workstation, or ends while a clinician is working
hazard: Someone else reads or writes under a clinician's sign-in, or a clinician loses unsaved work when signed out
cause: A page that polls in the background kept the session alive indefinitely (fixed); a sign-out for inactivity with no warning; a warning not seen; a clinician typing a long entry without saving
effect: A disclosure, or an entry made under the wrong person's name; or an entry lost and not re-entered
controls: Background looks (the patient page's minute poll of the record and allergies) are marked and never count as activity, in the hook and in the proxy, so the 900 s idle limit holds on an open page; two minutes before the limit the page shows an alert with the minutes left and a Stay signed in button (same-origin, no API call, not audited); the page's own clock of activity can only lag the server's, so the warning comes early, never late; the 8-hour absolute limit holds however active

title: A triage is made with the wrong flowchart or a missed discriminator
hazard: A patient is given a lower urgency than their presentation needs, or is seen late
cause: The wrong presenting-complaint flowchart is picked; a discriminator is skipped or answered from memory; the nurse is interrupted; a discriminator is read as absent when it was not asked
effect: A patient who needs urgent care waits longer than the target; harm from delay
controls: Planned, not built (TR-5, TR-7): a discriminator not asked is stored as not-assessed with a reason and never read as absent, so a missing assessment never lowers the category; the first applicable discriminator sets the suggestion; the nurse confirms or overrides with a reason; every triage is audited and append-only
residual: Nothing is built. No test. Ratings are proposed by the author and unreviewed; likelihood is a guess with no data from any site

title: Children and other groups MTS handles badly are under-triaged
hazard: A child, such as one with congenital heart disease, or a patient whose vital signs are abnormal but not part of the discriminators, is given a low category
cause: Published validation work reports under-triage for some groups, from abstracts only; the discriminators do not use vital signs; the tool is trusted over the patient's look
effect: Delayed assessment of a deteriorating patient
controls: Planned, not built (TR-9, TR-10): latest vitals and NEWS2 or a paediatric score shown beside the category, with a prompt, never an automatic change, when they point to higher urgency; a report of triage category against outcome by group

title: A triage category is changed silently or lost
hazard: The category on screen differs from what the nurse confirmed, or a re-categorisation leaves no trace
