title: A patient's request to correct a record is lost, mis-decided or not shown to readers
hazard: A record that is wrong stays wrong, a correction is applied on the wrong authority, or a reader acts on a record that is under dispute without being told
cause: The request is not seen by a clinician in time; a decision is made by the person who asked, or by a role that should not decide; a refusal loses the patient's statement of disagreement; a correction is made by editing instead of a new version; the notice of a pending, amended or refused request is not shown beside the record; the deadlines are wrong; a request or its words leak into the audit trail
effect: A clinician acts on a record the patient has said is wrong, or a patient's correction is silently dropped; a legal right to amend is not honoured
controls: Service (RC-4, 2026-10-27): the rules are pure and tested (`amendment.rs`): the decider is never the requester, every decision needs a non-blank reason, the applied version must be later than the disputed one so the record is corrected by a new version and never edited, nothing leaves a final state, one statement of disagreement is kept unedited; the store is append-only by trigger and every step keeps its event and author; the requester and the decider are the token and never the body; a deciding step needs the clinician role and a withdrawal or statement the patient role, so a patient cannot decide and a clinician cannot speak for the patient; a stale version is 409; the record-level decision applies in full (care relationship, purpose, consent) and a proxy has no scope for amendments so is refused; every write and its audit row are one transaction, and a write whose audit row cannot be written is refused and leaves nothing (audit-failure test); the audit row holds ids, kinds, versions and states, never the request text, a reason or a statement (tested)
residual: The JSON observation list carries the notice and the vitals section shows it (2026-10-27, English wording unreviewed), and the allergy list and its section carry it too (2026-10-27), and so do the FHIR Observation and AllergyIntolerance searches (2026-10-27, as English prose in `note`, accepted by the HL7 validator; not a coded extension, and no read by id or export exists yet); a clinician can decide a request in the UI (2026-10-27) and the request names the record it is about, but nothing checks the version typed; a patient can ask about a vital sign or an allergy from /my-record (2026-10-27, stubbed tests only, not seen with a real login; the clinician page was run once against the real service with login off); the open and overdue count shows only on that patient's page and nothing alerts across patients; a proxy cannot ask; nothing checks that an applied version really corrects the disputed field; only observations and allergies can be amended; who counts as a decider is just the clinician role; the proxy, adult-child and UK/GDPR rectification cases are not modelled; the 60 and 30 days follow HIPAA 164.526 as read by the author and are a guess, as is the grounds list; no clinician or privacy officer has reviewed any of it; not tested with a real Keycloak login; the FHIR notice is coded by an extension at a placeholder address that no consumer is known to read, so a reader that ignores unknown extensions still has only the text (2026-10-28)

title: A hazard is retired while it still applies
hazard: A hazard that still applies is taken off the active list, so the risk it records is no longer managed, watched or shown to the people who decide
cause: The wrong person retires it; evidence is missing, stale, altered or does not show what it claims; the officer who recorded the control also retires it; a retired hazard is not reopened when it is seen again; the register is edited or emptied afterwards; the Clinical Safety Officer role is given to a service account or to everyone
effect: An unsafe feature or workflow stays in use because its hazard looks closed; the safety case reports a risk that has not been controlled
controls: Service (AS-17, 2026-10-28): only the clinical-safety-officer role retires a hazard, and the check does not switch off when login is off, so with no token nobody retires (tested); a retirement without evidence is a 422, each item needs a kind, a reference, a past time and a SHA-256 (tested); whoever recorded a control cannot retire the hazard (tested); any writer reopens with a reason (tested); the register is append-only by trigger and the route has no delete (tested); the role is the token's and never the body's (tested); every step is audited with the evidence hashes and never the free text (tested); the table is in the personal-data inventory (census test)
residual: No clinical safety officer is named (OQ-2), so nobody can retire a hazard yet, and the role has no holder; a hash shows the evidence did not change after it was recorded, not that it is true, and an officer can still attach weak evidence; nothing re-checks evidence later (AS-18); the sign-off for the repository's own hazard log file is still by pull request only (AS-13); a one-person site fails the four-eyes rule; the register is not linked to feature gates (AS-18); the Keycloak role exists but no one holds it; the ratings are the author's proposals

title: A record served as FHIR R5 differs from the stored record
hazard: A partner or clinician reads a version of the record that has lost, changed or reshaped something the stored R4 record says
cause: The R4 to R5 conversion drops or retypes an element (a reaction, a unit, a range, the amendment notice, the 'not recorded' warning) and still answers; a retyped element is mapped wrongly; a search set loses its warning that an empty list is not a statement of none; the answer names the wrong release; the R5 route skips a gate, a consent check or an audit row that its R4 twin has; the partner treats the base R5 shape as a UK Core or US Core profile
effect: A clinician or a partner's system acts on a quieter or different record: an allergy without its reaction, a vital sign without its range, a disputed record shown as undisputed
controls: Service (IO-16, 2026-10-29): R5 is derived from the R4 answer by calling the R4 handler, so the gate, care relationship, purpose, consent and audit row are the R4 ones and there is no second set of converters (route census covers the five new routes); the conversion must report no loss and no warning, so a dropped or retyped element fails the response with a 500 outcome that names no value (tested with a planted field); the one retyping this service's R4 output needs (reaction.manifestation to a concept) is mapped and tested, and any other retyped element still fails; the allergy, observation (value, unit, range, amendment notice) and patient (merge link) bodies the service really writes are converted in tests; the 'not recorded', 'no known allergies' and empty-vitals warnings survive (tested); the HL7 validator accepts each converted body against R5 5.0.0 and refuses a broken one (CI); an Accept naming another release is a 406 and the capability statement says R5, reads only, base R5 with no UK Core or US Core claim (tested); no R5 write route exists
residual: The R4 to R5 differences were not read from the specification (IO-17); only what the converter reports and the validator checks is covered, so a semantic change that keeps the shape would pass; the Accept fhirVersion rule is built for R5 only, not R4; the conversion is by the fhir crate's element tables and one hand-written retyping, neither reviewed by a clinician or by HL7; no real partner has read the output; AuditEvent, Consent and Provenance are not served in R5; the amendment-notice extension URL is a placeholder; ratings are the author's proposals

title: An event leaves the service to a recipient who should not have it
hazard: A change to a patient's record is sent to a subscriber, webhook or other sink that the patient's consent, the recipient's role or the purpose of use does not allow, or is sent twice, or is lost
cause: A producer writes an event without the recipient's roles or purpose, or with the wrong ones; the delivery skips the consent check or the policy check that the read path makes; a consent lookup fails and the delivery goes ahead; the runner delivers an event whose transaction rolled back; a crash after a sink answers delivers again; a sink's error text carries patient data into the attempt table; an event stays pending for ever and nobody sees it
effect: A partner system or a person receives patient data the patient refused or the role may not see; a partner acts on a duplicate or a change that never happened; a change a partner needs never arrives and its copy of the record goes stale
controls: Service (OS-3, 2026-10-30; relayed by axa-outbox 0.2 since 2026-11-08): an event is written in the caller's transaction, and enqueue takes a transaction, not a pool, so a rollback removes it (tested); before a sink is called the relay makes the read path's own decision for the recipient in the claim's transaction, policy::evaluate with the recipient's roles and purpose and the patient's consent, and anything but a plain allow is a refusal that is audited and final, and nothing can put it back (tested for a refusing patient, a role the policy does not allow, and an allow that carries a masking obligation by construction); a failed death or consent lookup decides nothing and the event waits, never a delivery; a recipient has no care relationship, so a clinical read by a treating role is refused; the roles, purpose, resource and patient are stored in the payload under the fingerprint axa-outbox keeps, so an event whose stored payload was changed, even with the triggers turned off, is failed as tampered, never published, and audited (tested); events, payloads and attempts are insert-only under triggers that fire for every role and under replica mode, and the service does not start a relay without them (tested); a sink's failure is tried five times in all with a doubling wait, then left failed for a person, who releases it by name and reason (tested); a reason on an attempt is a code of at most 200 characters with no line breaks, and free error text is never stored; a payload over 64 KiB is refused with its transaction (tested); on shutdown the service stops serving, then the relay finishes the publish in progress and hands the rest of its batch back unsent, uncharged and unrecorded as sent, and one that has not stopped in 35 seconds is abandoned and logged (tested); delivery, refusal and a changed event are audit rows naming the event, never its content, committed with the outcome
residual: Nothing calls enqueue and no sink exists (IO-6), so no event leaves the service today and this hazard is about the mechanism, not a live flow; delivery is at least once (a relay that dies after a sink answers, or stalls past five minutes, sends again), so every sink must treat a repeat as a repeat and none is written yet; the roles and purpose are supplied by the producer and are not checked against a registered subscriber list; the decision is made when the event is claimed, so a consent withdrawn or a death reported between the claim and the sink's answer does not stop that delivery; a failed lookup is logged by the relay and leaves no attempt row; the delivery counters are counted before the outcome commits, so an outcome that fails to commit is still counted; no alert on events stuck failed (a gauge exists); no route lets a person release a failed event, and no one has been named to do it; payloads are stored in clear (sealing is off) and no deny list of field names is set; the waits between retries, a lost relay and the order per key are axa-outbox's and are tested there, not here; no clinician or privacy officer has reviewed the rules

title: A clinician is refused a request by a rate limit while treating a patient
hazard: A request that a clinician needs (a patient search, a record read, a compare at registration) is answered 429 and the screen shows an error or an empty result
cause: The limit is set too low for a busy ward or a shared login; many clinicians share one token subject; a script or a page that polls uses the whole allowance; a restart or a second replica changes who is counted; the UI treats a 429 as no result; an integration under one subject exhausts the allowance of the same subject's interactive use
effect: A clinician cannot see or register a patient for up to a minute, or reads an empty list as none, and delays or alters care
controls: Service (OS-2, 2026-10-30): defaults of 1200 requests and 120 compare calls per minute per subject, far above a person at a screen (a unit test counts a minute of five requests a second and a compare every two seconds without a refusal; the window is fixed, so every minute of a shift is counted alike); the answer is 429 with Retry-After and an error body, never an empty list, and the UI proxy passes both on and the shared status check turns a 429 into "This one was not carried out and nothing was changed" (UI unit tests); the limit counts only authenticated subjects and fails open when its table is full (since 2026-11-07 the counting is axa-ratelimit 0.2 with WhenFull::Allow, and a subject let through that way is counted in epr_rate_limit_overflowed_total; a unit test fills the table and sees a new subject let through); a bad setting stops the service starting rather than falling back to a low value; the first refusal in a window is audited and every one is counted in epr_rate_limited_total, so a rising count is visible
residual: The Clinical Safety Officer has not answered OQ-OS1 and has not reviewed the defaults; they are a guess at clinical use, not measured on a ward; the limiter ran in a test router, not in the running service; the UI says in words that a 429 was not carried out wherever a page uses the shared status check (24 call sites), but no page was driven to a 429 in a browser test, and a page that handles its own statuses was not audited; a shared login would pool its users into one allowance; the limiter can lift one subject's limit without a restart, but nothing in the service calls it, so in practice a restart is still needed; counts are per replica and lost on restart; an integration and a person under one subject share an allowance

title: A phone number is read under the wrong country's calling code
hazard: A local phone number is turned into an international one with a calling code that is not the site's, so two different people are scored as sharing a phone, or one person's two records are not
cause: A deployment enables the wrong pack, or two packs at once and names the wrong winner; a pack's calling code is wrong; the matcher's default of 44 stays in force where no pack is enabled; the pack was assembled from a public source and no person who works with that country's standards has checked it; a changed pack changes who is linked to whom without a replay
effect: A shared phone raises a pair's similarity toward Review or a link, or a real match is missed, so a clinician sees, or writes to, the wrong person's record or a split record
controls: Service and packs (OS-10, 2026-10-30): the calling code comes only from an enabled pack that loads; a pack with an unknown key, a code outside 1 to 999, a mismatched id, no vectors, or a vector the real matcher does not satisfy does not load and the service does not start; two enabled packs that disagree stop startup unless the deployer names the winner; with no pack enabled the matcher's own default applies, so behaviour is unchanged; a phone is never more than half the household evidence and a phone alone cannot auto-link (matcher controls under H-001); the rules have a SHA-256 logged at start; every shipped pack says reviewed none and a warning is logged for each enabled pack
residual: No person who works with either country's standards has reviewed a pack; the calling codes were taken from the E.164 list and not checked against a second source; the matcher's default of 44 means an empty list is the UK, not neutral, which misreads an Australian number at a deployment that forgets to enable au; the hash is logged but not written on records or link decisions, so a record does not say which rules applied; no dry run over a labelled corpus before a pack change; the pack was never enabled in a running service; only the phone code is a pack, every other country assumption in the equity audit remains in code

title: Two records are linked, or kept apart, on the strength of an Australian IHI
hazard: A deployment that enables the au pack lets a shared valid IHI link two records automatically, or two different valid IHIs forbid a link
cause: An IHI is mistyped or reused and still passes the check digit (one number in ten passes by chance); the prefix or check rule is wrong; a record carries the wrong person's IHI; the pack was assembled from a public source and no person who works with Australian standards has checked it; the IHI system URI differs from the one an Australian source sends, so the rule silently never fires
effect: A different person's record is linked to the patient's, or a true match is blocked and the patient is split into two records, so a clinician sees or writes to the wrong record
controls: Matcher 0.5.0 and packs (OS-10, 2026-10-31): the rule is off unless an enabled pack says use_ihi = true, so nothing changes for a deployment without au; a shared IHI links automatically only when the given name, family name and birth date are present and agree (a missing or different one goes to Review, as for the national health number); two different valid IHIs give NonMatch; an invalid IHI is ignored; a clash on either the national health number or the IHI forbids a link; the pack's own vectors (a shared number must link, different numbers must not) run through the real matcher at start and a failure stops the service; the rules have a SHA-256 logged at start
residual: The rule was tested against numbers the tests complete themselves and invented vectors, not an official test IHI; the prefix, length and Luhn rule were not re-read against the Digital Health specification; no person who works with Australian standards has reviewed the au pack; the IHI system URI was not checked against a real Australian feed; an IHI that is valid and wrong (a typo that keeps the check digit) is not detectable here; the hash is not written on the link decision; no dry run over a labelled corpus; the rule was never enabled in a running service; the three new conflict codes are translated by machine only

title: An audit row is not shown, or the audit chain cannot be checked, after partitioning or archiving
hazard: Audit rows moved to the archive are missed by a reader that does not use the all-rows view, or a write fails because no partition exists for its month, or the chain check cannot start after an archive
cause: The archive step is switched on and moves partitions that a patient or an investigator still needs; a partition for the current or next month is missing, so an insert fails and the access is refused; an anchor is wrong or lost, so the chain check starts from the wrong digest or fails; the archive schema is dropped or its tables are edited by someone with database ownership; the service is down longer than the months of partitions made ahead
effect: A patient is told the access log is complete when it is not; an investigator cannot see who read a record; the service refuses requests because it cannot audit them; a removed or altered archived partition is not noticed
controls: Service (OS-13, 2026-10-31): archiving is off unless EPR_AUDIT_ARCHIVE_AFTER_MONTHS is set, so by default every row stays in audit_events; the patient access log and the audit search read audit_events_all, which joins the live table and every archived partition and is rebuilt in the same transaction as each move (tested: an archived row is still found by both); partitions are made 24 months ahead by the migration, at start, every six hours and inside the archive step itself (migration 20, tested: a write and a verification work straight after an archive); archiving moves a whole partition, never deletes (the moved table keeps its append-only triggers, tested), writes an append-only anchor first (first prev_digest, last digest, row count), and only partitions that end at least the set number of months ago are touched; audit::verify_archive recomputes each archived table's chain from its anchor; the chain check and the next append start from the newest anchor (tested across a partition boundary, after an archive, and when the live table is empty); partitioning keeps the old rows and ids and attaches the old table as the first partition inside one transaction
residual: Any new reader of audit_events that does not use audit_events_all would miss archived rows (the chain check and append deliberately read audit_events and the anchors); the view is a UNION ALL that grows by one branch per archived partition and its speed over many archived partitions was not measured; audit::verify_archive checks an archived table against its anchor and GET /api/audit/verify calls it (tested: an edited archived row is a 409 naming the partition), but nothing runs the endpoint on a schedule, so a damaged archive is found only when someone verifies; the retention period is assumed (OQ-OS7), not set by governance; the migration was run on empty scratch databases and one with a few rows, not on a large production table (the attach scans every row once); a DROP of a partition by the database owner is not prevented; the service never ran the loop against a real clock at a month change; no person has reviewed the rules

title: A retried create writes the record twice, or a replayed answer shows something it should not
hazard: A create that is sent twice (a double click, a client that timed out and retried) is stored twice; or, once idempotency keys exist, a key is reused for a different request, a stored answer outlives its use, or a replay discloses without a trail
cause: A create route has no way to tell a retry from a second request; the Idempotency-Key header is optional, so a client that does not send it is not protected; the stored answer is a second copy of patient data; a key shared across subjects would hand one person another's answer; a failure after the write but before the answer is kept
effect: A duplicate allergy, observation, consent or relationship is shown to a clinician as two entries (a duplicated allergy can be read as two substances, a duplicated observation as a trend); or a patient's data stays in a second table longer than the record's own rules
controls: Service (OF-1, 2026-11-02; run by axa-idempotency since 2026-11-07): src/idempotency.rs. A POST under /api with an Idempotency-Key is run once per (token subject, key); the same key and request replays the kept answer with Idempotent-Replayed: true and writes nothing; a different method, path, query or body is a 422; a key still running, or whose answer was not kept, is a 409, and a run holds its key for the key's whole life (axa-idempotency's default from 0.2.0; the service never sets rerun_abandoned_after, which would allow a shorter lease, and a unit test pins it), so a run that may have written is never run again under its key; only a success is kept, a refusal releases the key; keys are per subject and expire after 24 hours, removed hourly; a replay is audited and is refused if the audit row cannot be written; a key check that fails refuses the request instead of running it unguarded, and the service does not start without its table. Tests: tests/http_idempotency.rs; the UI forwards a well-formed key and drops a malformed one (tests/unit/proxy-handler.test.ts).
residual: The header is optional, so a client that omits it is exactly as exposed as before. The UI sends a key on four creates (patient registration, allergy, relationship, consent) and not on the others (break-glass review, feed resolution, amendment, observation). A failure after the record is written but before the answer is kept leaves the key held (a retry is a 409, not a second write, until the key expires; axa-idempotency 0.1's default lease of a minute would have allowed a second write; 0.2.0 holds the key by default, and a shorter lease is never set here), but a 5xx after a successful write releases the key and a retry can write again. The stored answer is patient data kept for up to a day outside the record. /fhir/ creates are not covered. The sweep loop and a real crash between write and answer are not tested (a held key is, by setting its row) (per-subject separation is: tests/http_idempotency_roles.rs). Not accepted: only the Clinical Safety Officer accepts a hazard.

title: A referral outcome or decline is filed against the wrong referral, or against none, and the referrer is never told
hazard: An outcome, decline or interim note reaches the record but is not matched to the referral it answers, or is matched to the wrong one, so the referrer believes the loop is still open (or closed) when it is not
cause: The outcome carries no referral id, or a mistyped or reused one; a letter is filed by patient and date alone; two referrals of one patient to one service are told apart only by free text; a decline or outcome arrives after the referral was cancelled or redirected; an unmatched outcome is dropped, or sits where no one looks
effect: A result or a decision (an urgent finding, a refusal to see the patient) is not acted on: the referrer waits for a reply that has come, or stops waiting for one that has not; a patient is lost to follow-up; or an outcome is shown against another referral and acted on
controls: Store, routes and a clinician screen (CA-3 first to third slices, 2026-11-03; no queue or worklist yet): spec/interoperability/closed-loop-referral.md. One referral id set by the referrer and carried on every later message; an outcome whose id matches no referral, or whose referral is already ended, goes to a queue a person must clear and is never filed silently; a refused transition is an error, not a silent change (electronic-patient-record-domain/src/referral.rs, pure, tested); the append-only referral store (src/referrals_store.rs) enforces the sender's role and a note where the event needs one, refuses a stale version, and keeps every step (triggers refuse update, delete and truncate), tested in tests/referrals_store.rs; routes under /api/patients/{id}/referrals gated by role, care relationship and consent, every send, step, refusal and read audited with ids, states and the role but never the text (src/controllers/referrals.rs, tests/http_referrals.rs); the patient-page screen offers only the steps the service lists as next and shows the state in words, a cancellation as a request (ReferralsSection.svelte); the referral status is stored, not inferred; every match, mismatch and clearance is audited. The unmatched-outcome queue store (src/referral_unmatched.rs, tests/referral_unmatched.rs): an inbound message with no id, an unknown id or a step the table refuses is kept with a reason, never dropped and never matched by patient and date; a clearance is a new row recording who and why. Routes (src/controllers/referral_queue.rs, tests/http_referral_queue.rs): an integrator sends inbound messages, a clinical administrator reads and clears the queue, every receipt, view and clearance is audited with ids and kinds but never the text. To be built: the queue screen, a worklist count for the referrer, who owns the queue when the sender is another organisation (OQ-PC4, assumed), timeouts for an uncleared entry (PC-3). The three capped oldest-first lists (referral queue, feed refusals, break-glass reviews) now answer `more: true` when a row was left behind (PR-1; electronic-patient-record-domain/src/page.rs, tested with 51 entries in each store, tests/referral_unmatched.rs, tests/mllp_feed.rs, tests/break_glass_store.rs), and the break-glass and feed screens say so. A clinical-administrator screen lists the unmatched replies, with the open count in the navigation on admin pages, and clears them with a reason (electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/src/routes/admin/referral-queue/+page.svelte, lib/referral-queue.ts, tests/e2e/patients.spec.ts). The referrer's worklist (backend, 2026-11-03): a referral the recipient declined, redirected, deferred, asked about, reported on or completed, or where the patient did not attend, waits on the sender's list until the sender acknowledges that version, and a later version waits again (src/referral_worklist.rs, tests/referral_worklist.rs, tests/http_referral_worklist.rs). Assumed (OQ-PC5). A "Replies to referrals you sent" screen lists them with a navigation count on that page and the patient record, and "Mark as seen" acknowledges the version shown (electronic-patient-record-ui-with-svelte/src/routes/referrals/+page.svelte, lib/referral-worklist.ts, tests/e2e/patients.spec.ts). Timeouts (PC-3, first slice): a referral with no answer, or accepted with no outcome, for longer than the period configured for its priority (EPR_REFERRAL_TIMEOUTS, no default, checked at start-up) is listed on the sender's worklist, and the list names the priorities with no period (src/referral_timeouts.rs, tests/referral_worklist.rs).
residual: Only the store and the routes are implemented: the routes take a step by id, but no outcome is matched from an inbound message, and the unmatched-outcome queue has routes and an administrator screen but no worklist count for the referrer, so an entry waits until an administrator looks, and nothing times it out; the recipient is any other permitted subject, not proved to be the named team (OQ-PC2 assumed); until the queue and the screens are built the hazard is unmitigated in use. The state table is a proposal from one unreviewed source and has not been checked against IHE 360X. A referral id typed wrongly by a sender that is itself a real referral will match the wrong one; only a person can catch that. Timeouts exist only if a deployment sets EPR_REFERRAL_TIMEOUTS, and a priority with no period never times out (the screen says which); no appointment-date timeout; nobody but the sender is told. The queue now has an administrator screen and a count, but the referrer's worklist has a screen, but the count shows only on that page and the patient record, so a referrer who opens neither is not told; the owner of a queue entry is not built, so an entry waits until an administrator opens the screen. A colleague covering for the sender sees nothing (OQ-PC5). Not accepted: only the Clinical Safety Officer accepts a hazard.

title: The ETH security label is read as ethnicity, not substance use
hazard: A record or consent rule labelled ETH is treated with the wrong meaning
cause: policy.rs maps the code ETH to Label::Ethnicity, but HL7 defines ETH as substance abuse information sensitivity; SUD is the only other substance code handled
effect: Substance-use information from another system is shown unmasked to nurses and allied health; a patient's consent rule naming ETH means something other than the patient was told
controls: policy.rs now reads ETH as substance abuse, with the same roles as SUD. A test pins each label code to its HL7 meaning, and another requires the two substance labels to unmask alike
residual: The pin is written by hand from the FHIR R4 value set and is not checked against HL7. Who sees SUD and ETH is itself a first draft with no clinical review

title: A death on an inbound HL7 message is dropped silently
hazard: An ADT message says the patient has died, and the record does not change
cause: The mapper read PID-3, 5, 7, 8, 11 and 13 and warned on bad values, but never read PID-29 or PID-30, and the record has no concept of death
effect: The sender is answered as if all was well; the person stays alive in the record, so contact can continue and a proxy continues
controls: The mapper now reads PID-29 and PID-30. A message reporting a death stores a report from the feed and is answered AA; a message that cannot be applied says its death was not recorded and waits in the feed queue, as does a repeat of a report a person withdrew. A date that cannot be stored becomes a report with no date. A proxy has no relationship once a death is confirmed, and a withdrawal restores it. FHIR sends a confirmed death as deceased[x] and an unconfirmed report as a tag; a FHIR write with a new deceased[x] gets a 422. death.rs and death_store.rs hold the rules and the store, and staff can report and act on a death through the routes in controllers/deaths.rs, and the banner shows a report and says if it could not check. The feed is off unless EPR_MLLP_BIND is set; a confirmed death stops a proxy and the patient's own login, worked out on each request so a withdrawal restores them (2026-11-05). Clinicians, nurses and administrators see every report that waits, oldest first, with a count in the navigation, and the on-duty clinician is accountable (OQ-BV4, 2026-11-06)
residual: The list has no push: someone must open a page to see it. The rota belongs to workforce planning management and the service will not hold one (decided 2026-11-06), so it cannot say who holds the on-duty role or whether anyone does; a shift with no holder has nobody accountable, nothing here says so, and no link from a workforce system exists: the role is given by hand. No time limit is set for a report to wait. The outbox runner holds any event about the patient, but nothing enqueues yet, so only the banner holds contact in use. A hold also stops anything that should reach someone after a death. An A03 discharge for a death is refused and says so, but nothing is recorded. A false confirmation locks a proxy out with no explanation. A patient's own login continues after a death. A wrong death from a feed now shows in the banner of a living patient until a clinician withdraws it. Tried only against test messages, and no other system has read the FHIR tag; a person wrongly confirmed as dead loses their own record until a clinician withdraws it; a proxy can read the record of someone who has died until a person confirms the report

title: A temporary name for an unknown patient is read as real identity evidence
hazard: An unconscious or unidentified patient is given a temporary name, and the matcher treats it as a real name
cause: The placeholder rule covers words such as unknown and unk, but a temporary name in the safer format a 2018 national patient safety alert on naming unknown patients recommends, with an estimated birth date, looks real; nothing marks a temporary identity
effect: Two unknown patients, or an unknown patient and a real one, could be linked or offered as a match, with the risk of wrong-patient care in an emergency
controls: The service uses matcher 0.6.0. A person sets temporary_identity at registration or on edit; the matcher then withholds names and birth dates and never auto-links. The banner, search results and FHIR meta.tag show it. Ending it needs a reason, an HL7 message never ends it, and a merge with no other evidence needs the real details first
residual: The flag works only if a person sets it, and nothing checks the name format or that the name is a temporary one. A writer that drops the flag and gives a reason still ends it. The banner text is English only. Lists other than patient search do not show it, and it is not carried to another hospital. No clinician has reviewed the wording or who may end it

title: A communication need or adjustment is missing, stale or not seen
hazard: A person who needs an interpreter, large print or step-free access does not get it, or staff act on a need that no longer applies
cause: Never recorded; recorded and not looked at; the review date passed; ended by mistake; a note holds the wrong language; a refused consent hides it; two records of one person hold different needs before a merge
effect: A person cannot follow what is said and cannot give real consent, misses care or is harmed by an instruction not understood
controls: A coded catalogue, with a language required for a spoken interpreter; append-only versions with a reason, and ending one is final; a date to check it with the person, and overdue worked out on each read; every read and write audited with no code, note or reason in the audit row (2026-11-05); an adjustment informs staff and changes nothing by itself; the banner shows what stands and an overdue check, a failed look says so, and an empty list says none recorded and that this does not mean there are none; a list across patients of overdue checks, owned by the on-duty clinician (OQ-PX2), oldest date first, says when it is cut, holds no code, note or reason, and marks a person with a report of death standing (PX-2, 2026-11-06); the same need recorded by two people at one moment is stored once, so that ending it ends it (2026-11-25)
residual: The catalogue and its words are mine and the role table is a first draft; no clinician, disabled person or interpreter has reviewed them; nothing tells anyone that a review is overdue: the on-duty clinician has to open the list, there is no count in the navigation and no push, and a shift with no holder of the role leaves it unowned and nothing says so, because the rota belongs to workforce planning; nothing records who took a check on; a patient can change their own needs at once, with no approval and nothing telling staff, so a need staff believe still applies can be ended; a list that holds only a date cannot put the most serious need first; no national code list; a need can be recorded wrongly and is shown as recorded

title: Every clinician behind one address is locked out after a few failed tokens
hazard: Requests from a client address are refused for up to 15 minutes after that address was answered a set number of 401s, and the address is shared by many people
cause: LOCKOUT_CLIENT_ADDRESS_AFTER_COUNT is set where the service sees the UI's server, a ward's NAT or a proxy not listed in TRUSTED_PROXIES as the client, so every user is one address; expired or mistyped tokens from a few users, a page polling with an expired session, or an attacker sending bad tokens from the same address, reach the count; the count is set too low
effect: No clinician using the system through that address can read or record anything for up to 15 minutes, and care is delayed or decided without the record
controls: Service (OS-2, 2026-11-09): off unless LOCKOUT_CLIENT_ADDRESS_AFTER_COUNT is set, and the service logs a warning at start when it is on; only a 401 counts, so a valid token never counts; the probes are never refused; the answer is 429 with Retry-After and a message that names the lockout, never an empty list, and the UI's shared status check says a 429 was not carried out; an IPv6 address is counted by its /64; the table fails open when full (axa-ratelimit WhenFull::Allow), counted in epr_rate_limit_overflowed_total; a bad setting stops the service starting; the first refusal of an address in a window is audited with the address, and every refusal is counted in epr_lockouts_total (tests/http_lockout.rs; a run of the real binary with login on: three 401s, then 429)
residual: The UI's server sends the browser's address as X-Forwarded-For (since 2026-11-09), but the service believes it only when TRUSTED_PROXIES lists the UI's server, and only compose.yaml does (since 2026-11-09: the UI container at a fixed 10.89.240.250 and TRUSTED_PROXIES that one address); no other deployment does, so turning it on behind the UI without that locks out everyone at once, and nothing stops a deployment doing so but the warning and the spec; a TRUSTED_PROXIES that also lists something a browser can reach the service from lets that browser choose its address and lock out a clinician's; there is no way to lift a lockout but waiting or a restart; the window is fixed at 15 minutes; an attacker who can send requests from a clinician's address can lock that address out on purpose; counts are per replica and lost on restart; no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer has reviewed whether it should be on anywhere

title: A result changed after sign-off is taken as signed
hazard: A clinician or a reader sees a tick on a result whose value has changed since it was signed off
cause: A sign-off stored against the result rather than its version; an amended or corrected version arriving after sign-off; a screen that shows only the newest sign-off; a feed that rewrites a result in place
effect: A corrected or newly abnormal value goes unseen by the clinician responsible and is not acted on
controls: Service (WL-1, 2026-11-09): a sign-off names the version it was made on and is append-only; a result changed after sign-off reads changed-since-sign-off with the signed version shown beside the current; signing a version that is no longer current is a 409 naming the current one; a version entered in error has nothing to sign; versions are append-only and move forward only (never back to preliminary), each change with a reason; the audit trail names results and versions and never a value (tests/http_results.rs); a signature meets the review obligation of the version it named and no later one: a correction that is abnormal or critical, or any correction after a signature, files the result again, so a rule's task reopens once; a signature and a correction that race are one after the other (tests/tasks_store.rs, 2026-11-25)
residual: No screen shows results yet; no feed files them (only a clinician can, by hand), so the inbox routing to the ordering clinician, abnormal-first ordering and escalation of an unsigned abnormal result (OR-4) are not built and a result can wait unsigned unseen; nobody is told when a signed result changes; no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer has reviewed the states or who may sign

title: Unreviewed Welsh wording misleads a clinician
hazard: A clinician reading the UI in Welsh acts on a machine-written word that means something else
cause: The Welsh table (cy-001) is machine-written and no Welsh speaker or Welsh-speaking clinician has read it; clinical terms (vital signs and allergies and entered in error and the death statuses and break-the-glass) may be wrong or ambiguous; sentences built from parts keep English word order; service messages stay English beside Welsh
effect: A value or status is misread and a decision is made on it; a warning is not understood
controls: UI (WL-8, 2026-11-09): every page in a machine-written unreviewed locale says so in that language and in English with a link to the same page in English; REVIEW in src/lib/i18n.ts records cy-001 as machine-written and unreviewed and a test fails if any locale claims review without a named reviewer and a date; every key exists in Welsh with its placeholders (type and unit tests); the words least sure of are listed for the reviewer at the top of strings.cy.ts; governance/translation-review.md names the table
residual: No Welsh speaker or Welsh-speaking clinician has reviewed any string; the Welsh Language Standards for health bodies were not read; nothing stops a deployment using cy-001 clinically but this notice and the NOT FOR CLINICAL USE notice; API problem text and service messages stay English; the matcher knows no anglicised Welsh names (ap Rhys and Price go to review) and holds no address lines

title: An assessment is read under the wrong form or a draft form is taken as approved
hazard: A reader sees answers beside questions they were not given under, or acts on a form nobody approved
cause: A new form version changes a question's words or choices and old answers are shown under the new words; a form is used before a named clinician approves it; an unanswered question is read as no
effect: A risk is missed or overstated and care is planned on it
controls: Service (WL-3, 2026-11-09): every assessment keeps its form id and version and is shown with that version's questions and words; a form version is data read into the build and versions must follow one another; a form without both an approver and a day is shown as a draft (approved false) with the newest version named beside it; every question is answered once or marked absent with a reason, never blank; the records are append-only (tests/http_assessments.rs)
residual: The only form is a project-written example and not a clinical tool; nothing stops the catalogue gaining a version that removes an older one except the version rule and review; no screen shows the draft flag yet; no correction or entered-in-error; no licensed tool (OQ-M2 and OQ-WL2); no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer has reviewed it

title: A suspicion pathway gives the wrong target date or priority
hazard: A clinician, the referrer's list or the PAS shows a due day or priority that does not match the condition's pathway
cause: A figure in the pathway catalogue is wrong or out of date (the built-in figures came from search summaries of guidelines); a draft pathway is used as if approved; the wrong band is chosen; a factor that raises the priority is not recorded; due days are counted in another zone's days than the site's (EPR_SITE_TIME_ZONE unset at a site outside UTC); a pause in the clock is not modelled; a pathway without an interval is read as no hurry; a subtype code from one list is read against another
effect: A patient with a suspected serious condition is seen late
controls: Service (RS-6, 2026-11-09): pathways are versioned data read into the build and a bad catalogue stops the build's tests; a pathway without both an approver and a day is reported as a draft; a pathway with bands refuses a suspicion without one and a band that follows a measured value refuses grounds that are not a result; an unknown factor is refused; a pathway needing the person's agreement refuses a suspicion without it; a pathway with no interval must say why; a subtype (a primary cancer site, a type of dementia) is taken only from the pathway version's own list, stored with its scheme so a code from another list is never relabelled and named in the plan from that same list, and a pathway whose list is required refuses a suspicion without one (RS-5, 2026-11-10); due days and overdue are counted in the site's time zone, named in the plan, and a zone that is not an IANA name stops the service starting (2026-11-10); each rule has a test (pathways::tests)
residual: Every built-in pathway is a draft written from search summaries of NICE and Welsh Government pages, not the pages; no clinician has approved any; the plan is shown read-only under each referral (2026-11-10), with a draft pathway marked as a draft; an outcome does not stop a target (RS-3); the PAS clock is authoritative and not read here (PA-15); no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer has reviewed it

title: A suspicion on a referral is lost or changed unseen or revealed to a patient who was not told
hazard: The reason a referral is urgent, or the day its clock started, is missing or different from what the referrer recorded; or the patient learns of a suspected condition from the record before anyone has told them
cause: The suspicion is held as free text in the referral reason; an amendment rewrites the point of suspicion without a reason; two writers amend at once; the suspicion is read through the patient portal; the audit trail or access log names the suspected condition
effect: A patient with a suspected serious condition is seen late, or is distressed by learning of it from a screen
controls: Service (RS-1, 2026-11-09): one suspicion per referral, append-only by trigger, version 1 as raised and every later version an amendment with a reason (a database CHECK), an amendment that changes nothing refused, a stale version 409; each version shows the fields it changed and its own plan; the point of suspicion cannot be in the future; grounds of kind result must name a result on this patient's record; a referral reached through another patient is a miss; the patient-access purpose is refused (no patient view until RS-4); the audit row holds ids and versions and changed field names, never the pathway or the condition; triage and rebooking leave it untouched, and a referral that replaces a redirected one (replaces, once, same patient) carries its current suspicion as version 1 in the same transaction, naming where it came from, with the point of suspicion unchanged and a referral-sent clock counted from the first referral (RS-2); a suspicion ends only with an outcome (confirmed with the diagnosis, ruled out with who and on what, withdrawn with a reason), once, after which it cannot be amended; a missed appointment, a decline, a cancellation or a redirect never ends it; a referral that has ended with its suspicion open is on the referrer's worklist (open-suspicion) until an outcome is recorded and acknowledging the referral does not remove it (RS-3); an outbound event that names a suspected condition (names_suspicion_of) is refused at the outbox gate to a patient or proxy unless the referral's current suspicion says the patient was told, read when the event is sent (RS-4, tests/outbox_store.rs); an outcome recorded in error is marked entered in error by its seq with a reason, which reopens the suspicion (amendable, back on the worklist, open to a new outcome) and keeps the first outcome and the reason in the history, append-only, and a stale seq is 409 (RS-7, 2026-11-10) (tests/http_suspicions.rs); an amendment, an outcome and the withdrawal of an outcome take turns on a referral, so that none is stored on what another is changing at the same moment (2026-11-25)
residual: A read-only screen shows each referral's suspicion (2026-11-10), with the not-told warning, the draft note, the due days and the outcome, and a form raises one under the newest pathway versions with no preselected answer for whether the patient was told, a required subtype, a band or the person's agreement (2026-11-10), and forms record its outcome (no kind preselected, each kind asking for what it carries, against the version on screen) and mark an outcome entered in error with a reason (2026-11-10), and a form corrects whether the patient was told, the point of suspicion and the instruction with a reason, sending the rest unchanged under the same pathway version (2026-11-10), but no screen corrects the other fields, the point of suspicion is typed in the reader's own time, and its Welsh is machine-written and unreviewed; a replacement made without naming the redirected referral it replaces starts with no suspicion; any treating role may mark an outcome entered in error, with no second person, and a PAS stop already sent cannot be undone there; the open-suspicion worklist reaches only the referrer, not the recipient or a team; the outbound check relies on the sender setting names_suspicion_of, and nothing finds a payload that names the condition without it; no letter, portal or text sender exists yet; the PAS does not receive it (RS-5); any treating role with a care relationship may amend it, not only the referrer; no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer has reviewed it

title: A late HL7 message undoes a newer change to a patient's details
hazard: A delayed or resent update from a feed replaces a newer one, so a corrected name, address or phone number goes back to the old value
cause: A sender resends after a lost acknowledgement; messages from one sender arrive out of order over two connections; a queue behind the sender releases old messages after an outage
effect: A clinician or a letter reaches a patient through an old address or phone number, or reads a name that had been corrected
controls: Each update the feed applies records its event time (EVN-2, or MSH-7) per feed and patient in an append-only table; under a lock per feed and patient, an update older than the newest one applied is not applied and is kept in the work queue for a person, answered AR with a time-free reason; the same time is not older; another feed's times do not count (IH-5)

title: A task rule makes the wrong task, no task, or a reminder that hides a real one
hazard: A rule built into or loaded by the service gives a team the wrong task, misses a result that needed one, or a backlog of reminders after downtime buries the one that matters
cause: A rule's conditions are wrong or too narrow; a holiday or weekend is missing from the site calendar so a due day is late; a rule is approved without clinical review; reminders that fell during downtime all fire at once
effect: A clinician does not review an abnormal result in time, or wastes time on tasks that do not need doing
controls: A rule creates a task and nothing else: no message to a patient, no change to the record (an unknown key or action stops the rule file loading); only an approved rule makes tasks, and every rule built in is a draft until OQ-TL1 says who approves; the dry run shows a draft's tasks; a rule and every task it makes name the rule version; tasks are written in the same transaction as the event's write, with audit rows, or not at all (TL-14); duplicate rules are refused when read; working days skip weekends and site holidays; each reminder is decided once, and a late one is sent once or skipped with the reason recorded (TL-4); events named by the rule cancel only their own record's open tasks The site's holidays (EPR_SITE_HOLIDAYS) are checked at start-up and a day that does not parse stops the service, as does a rules file that does not load; a result with no abnormal flag carries no abnormal fact, so silence never matches a rule as normal; a result entered in error raises nothing. An observation raises out of range only when its flag says so (no value or no range is no flag), and only when the last version was not out of range, so a re-save makes no second task; entered in error cancels its tasks. A referral raises a step on each state it reaches and closed at an end, so a task asked for at triage can be cancelled when the referral ends. A team's list and a close are for those who hold the team's role, refused and audited otherwise, and a rule whose team is no role stops the service; a close needs a reason and the version read; the dry run marks drafts, writes nothing, and refuses a fact the event does not carry. The reminder sender decides each reminder once (a second replica or run leaves it), a reminder missed while nothing ran is sent once or skipped with the reason as its rule says, a bad interval stops the start, and the start warns when the sender is off. A result entered in error after filing raises result-entered-in-error, which the built-in draft names, so its task is cancelled; a result amended to abnormal raises result-filed once. A site's rules file (EPR_TASK_RULES_FILE) is checked exactly as the built-in catalogue, a fault stops the start naming the file, and the start logs how many rules run and how many are approved. The screen shows a task overdue once the site's day passes its due day, says when a list is cut, and never shows a refused list as empty; a result's task names the version that raised it; critical is a fact apart from abnormal, and after_sign_off is a fact; an open task is not made twice (2026-11-25)
residual: Results raise their events, but every built-in rule is a draft, so a running service makes no task yet; a result amended from abnormal back to normal leaves its task open for a person to close; the reminder sender is off unless EPR_TASK_REMINDER_MINUTES is set, and a sent reminder only marks the list (nobody is alerted); a team is a role (OQ-TL3), so a task cannot go to one ward or clinic; who approves a rule is open (OQ-TL1); no clinician or Clinical Safety Officer has reviewed it; a site's rules file may name its own approver, and nothing checks who that is (OQ-TL1); no covering recipient, acknowledgement time or escalation exists (AG-1, OQ-AG1); a task is only a team's list entry

title: A phone shows the wrong patient, or keeps a patient's record after it leaves the clinician's hands

The scaffold's Banner text is tested to keep every part whole and to say not available for an absent part. Threat model for a lost or shared device written (governance/mfa-plan.md, governance/data-flow.md, 2026-11-23): a phone unlock is not the service's second factor; no offline_access refresh token; one user per install; revocation or wipe on report. effect: A wrong or late treatment; an incompatible transfusion; a retracted cause that a hidden problem still names
controls: The care team is told how many are withheld; a partial list never says not recorded, none active or that blood groups agree; break-glass shows everything; another clinician may lift a label; labels are on three lists only and not on allergies
residual: No screen shows these lists or says that any is withheld; a refusal of consent that names a label is not lifted in an emergency (OQ-PI8); nobody is asked to review a label; who sees each label is the author's draft; severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: A label is missing, wrong or lost, so that a sensitive entry is shown
hazard: An entry that should carry a label does not, or carries it in one place and not in another
cause: Nobody adds it; it is lifted by mistake; the same fact is written elsewhere (a referral, an observation, free text) where nothing carries a label; an output added later does not mask
effect: Harm to the patient (discrimination, violence, loss of trust)
controls: A label is lifted only by a clinician who did not add it, with a reason that is kept; what happened to a label cannot be changed or removed; a label follows its entry through a merge; a code this version does not know withholds; a census fails when labels reach another file or a new output route is added
residual: None is added automatically, so every label depends on a person (OQ-PI7); free text is not looked at; nothing compares the same fact in two places; an answer kept for a retried write is not masked again; severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: An older build serves a newer database
hazard: A build that does not know what a newer one withholds or requires serves the record
cause: A release is undone, or an old server restarts, after the database was migrated; production does not migrate at start, so nothing compared the two
effect: An entry with a security label is shown to everyone; a write breaks a rule that the newer build keeps
controls: start refuses a database with a migration the build does not know, and one with a migration not applied; a setting for a person who decides that an outage is worse, which warns
residual: A build from before this check does not make it; a server already running when the database is migrated is not stopped; a refused start is an outage until the newer build is started, so a bad release has to be fixed forward; severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: A merge joins two people and one has the other's refusal of treatment
hazard: A refusal made by one person is shown and followed for another, or a refusal is left behind when two records are separated
cause: A merge of records of two people, or an unmerge that leaves a refusal recorded since the merge on the wrong record; the person who merges cannot read refusals and is not asked
effect: A person is treated against what they refused, or is denied treatment they accepted because another person refused it
controls: a merge stops until a person names every refusal of the record merged away (refusals_seen); an unmerge stops for each recorded on the survivor since the merge; the stop names ids and never the words; the other record's refusal is shown as another record's (from_merged_record)
residual: Nothing makes the person who merges look at the words (an administrator has no right to read them: the person asked is whoever they ask); a refusal recorded on the survivor before the merge is not asked about on unmerge; no screen exists yet (RF-7); severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: "None recorded" is read as "none" for a refusal of treatment
hazard: A clinician takes an empty list of refusals as proof that there are none, or an unreadable one as empty
cause: The list is empty because nothing was recorded, the record is another person's, an error hid the list, or everything recorded was withdrawn or entered in error
effect: A person who refused a treatment is given it because no refusal was shown
controls: the list carries a summary that says none-recorded, recorded or all-withdrawn, and the words say what this record knows and never none; a refusal entered in error is left out of it, a doubted one is counted
residual: Only the API is built: the screen and the banner that must say it in words, and must say louder that a list could not be read, are RF-7; a person who is not a clinician reads none; severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: A withdrawal of a refusal of treatment is lost, or is taken to end it without a rule
hazard: Someone hears a person take back a refusal and it is not kept, or it is stored as ending the refusal where the place's law does not say that it does
cause: A withdrawal is spoken or by conduct and nobody records it; the record is set to withdrawn by habit
effect: A refusal that still stands is ignored, or one that was taken back is followed
controls: a withdrawal that was heard is kept as heard, with who noticed it and when; with no rule in force it is stored as doubted and never as withdrawn; a refusal is never removed, and what was said is a new version
residual: No rule file is read by the service yet (RF-3 is a library), so a withdrawal never ends a refusal here and everything stays doubted until a clinician looks; a doubted refusal is not told apart from one that stands by anything but its state; severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: An order, or another person's word, is shown as the patient's own refusal
hazard: A clinician's order, a relative's report or a card found with an unknown person is recorded as the patient's decision
cause: The kind of refusal is not asked or not read; a card is filed under a record whose identity is temporary
effect: A relative's word is followed as the patient's, or the patient's own is dismissed as a relative's
controls: who said it is kept apart from whom it is about (said_by must fit kind); a representative or a parent needs a power seen; a card that was not seen is never certainly theirs; identity uncertain is counted in the summary
residual: The rules are in the domain library tests; whether a person has power is the clinician's word and is not checked; no screen shows the difference yet (RF-7); severity and likelihood are the author's proposal

title: An answer about an emergency is wrong, guessed or read as more than it is
hazard: A grant says that a life is at risk, or that the patient cannot be asked, when that is not so; or a reviewer reads the answers as proof
cause: The opener picks an answer to get past the form; the form chooses one for them; the answers are read as a decision about the patient; what the patient said is lost
effect: A record is opened without need and the patient's wish is not heard; a reviewer passes a grant that should not have been opened; a later rule that lifts a refusal on these answers acts on a guess
controls: each answer is required, not-known is one, and nothing is chosen for the opener; what the patient said is required when they could be asked and refused otherwise; the answers are held with the grant, cannot change when the same person asks again, and are shown to the reviewer; a grant from before the question reads as not asked; nothing is worked out from a diagnosis, an age or the reason; what a grant lifts does not depend on the answers (OQ-PI8)
residual: Nobody checks an answer against the record; the reason and what was said are free text; the questions are the author's wording, and the Welsh is machine-written; no clinician has timed the form in an emergency; severity and likelihood are the author's proposal
